title: SharedPade _toeplitz_block off-by-one: d=1 fails to reduce to scalar GGT (m,m) on transcendental jets
description: CONFIRMED empirically + fix validated (worklog 065, sweep C1). src/SharedPade.jl:117 builds the shared-denominator Toeplitz block one Taylor coeff too low: idx=m+rr-cc+1 gives blk[1,1]=c_m (an (m-1,m) window), but the SP.1.1 / ADR-0019 contract and the scalar GGT (m,m) require c_{m+1} (RobustPade.jl:413-414; padeapprox.m:89,92). Invisible on exact-rational test jets (the true Q annihilates BOTH windows; every shared_pade_test.jl oracle AND the determinant Oracle-2 share the same off-by-one block), but bites on transcendental jets: 5-50% denominator error on exp/log1p and the numerator degree collapses by 1 — the real VectorStepper workload, adaptive m per step, hence intermittent discontinuity in vector trajectories. FIX: :117 +1 -> +2 AND raise the jet guard :175 from >=m+1 to >=2m+1 (the corrected block reads c_2m; fail loud per Rule 1); also fix the _toeplitz_block docstring arithmetic at :111 (says c_{m+r-c}, the slice is c_{m+r-c+1}). TEST: transcendental d=1 oracle comparing shared_denominator_pade([jet],m).Q to robust_pade(jet,m,m;:svd).b — the ONLY independent oracle (NOT the determinant oracle, which shares the bug). Probe: external/probes/sharedpade-offbyone-confirm/confirm.jl. Validated: +2 -> bit-exact on exp/log1p for all m, zero regression on the rational control. Likely root of symptom beads padetaylor-unk and padetaylor-0o9.
notes: RESOLVED (worklog 066, workflow wf_f81c8ec1-ee9, unanimous 3-judge consensus + sympy). ROOT CAUSE = target-approximant CONFLATION, not an index typo: pillar-A findings:407-411 faithfully transcribes Mano-Tsuda's minimal type-II = the OFF-DIAGONAL (m-1,m) window (top-left c_m, +1), then §3/§7 silently grafts GGT's m-rows row-count and asserts it = the GGT DIAGONAL (m,m) (top-left c_{m+1}, +2). The two differ by one numerator degree. Binding spec = ADR-0019/SP.1.1/docstring (diagonal (m,m)); the findings doc is the one to AMEND. CORRECT WINDOW = c_{m+1} (+2) at EVERY d. Fix = (A) :117 +1->+2; (C) docstring arithmetic :27/:34/:105-112 c_{m+r-c}->c_{m+r-c+1} (line 111 1-based->subscript mis-conversion rationalized the bug); (D) DO NOT touch _upper_block (sympy: already correct degree-m numerator under +2); (E) bump determinant Oracle 2 oracle.jl:160 +1->+2 + fix its docstring :92-98 (it mirrors the bug, can't catch it) — the only window-independent d=1 oracle is the transcendental robust_pade(jet,m,m;:svd) comparison (added as SP.1.7). JET GUARD :175: KEEP >=m+1 (do NOT raise to 2m+1 — robust_pade zero-pads short jets per RobustPade.jl:378, so raising breaks the d=1 bit-identity; the +2 block zero-pads gracefully). C1 depends on C2 (3p9c) for the d>=2 vector suite to pass.
close_reason: Shipped in commit 127edae (worklog 067). C1: +2 GGT (m,m) window, mutation-proven via transcendental SP.1.7. C2: graceful reduction (rho>=m_cur accept incl. full-rank least-squares) + z^λ cancellation + Q=1 Taylor fallback, mutation-proven. Meromorphic oracles GREEN (℘/Calogero/KKG/vector-path-network), no throws. Entire/regular-jet accuracy cost (grows with d; NY A4 ~6e-6) documented with honest tolerance updates; recovery deferred to ADR-0028 dispatch bead.

title: Phase 12: Dispatcher — compose PathNetwork + EdgeDetector + BVPSmooth into unified IVP/BVP solver
description: Tier-3 composition layer. Stitches PathNetwork (pole-rich regions, IVP) + BVPSmooth (smooth regions, BVP) into one PadeTaylorRegionSolution covering an arbitrary 2D complex-plane domain. Inputs: a problem, a grid, and tunables. Outputs: per-grid-point (u, u', region_classification) where region is :ivp / :bvp / :uncovered. Architecture per docs/adr/0004-path-network-architecture.md (Tier-3 deferral) and docs/unified_path_network_spec.md §8. Edge-detector dependency: padetaylor-c2p. Newton-BVP dependency: BVP module shipped at commit cc7d8ca. Unblocks: figure_catalogue.md §6 Tier-3 figures (FW2011 Fig 4.1/4.5/4.6, FW2014 Fig 10/11/12/16/25, FW2015 Fig 7/8/9/11, RF2014 Fig 2/7/15).
notes: v1 SCOPE (committed 2026-05-13): 1D ordered-chain dispatcher composing IVPSegment <-> BVPSegment with junction derivative-match diagnostic per FW2011...md:192 (tol 1e-7). Public API: dispatch_solve(prob, f_bvp, df_du_bvp, segments; ...) -> DispatcherSolution. Each segment is IVPSegment(z_end) or BVPSegment(z_end, u_b, N). Callable sol(z) -> (u, u', region). Tests: DP.1.1 single-IVP passthrough, DP.1.2 single-BVP passthrough, DP.2.1 IVP->BVP junction derivative-match, DP.3.1 IVP->BVP->IVP three-segment (FW 2011 §4.4), DP.4.1 fail-fast guards, DP.5.1 mutation-proof. v2 DEFERRED: 2D lattice dispatcher with automatic edge detection (5-point Laplacian per FW2011...md:204-208, threshold 0.001), per-row 2D smooth-band filling, EdgeDetector module (padetaylor-c2p) consumed at that point. Asymptotic IC providers (InitialConditions module) deferred separately.

title: BVP module: Chebyshev-Newton spectral collocation per FW 2011 §3.2 / FFW 2017
description: Roll-our-own ~150 LOC Julia BVP solver. Spec: Chebyshev extrema nodes t_j=cos(jπ/N), analytic D₂ matrix (Weideman-Reddy / Trefethen SMIM ch.6), Newton iter with analytic Jacobian (PI: ∂F/∂u = 12u, diagonal mod of D₂), barycentric eval to fine lattice (Berrut-Trefethen). Generic in T<:Number for Float64 + BigFloat + Complex{T}; Arb routes through BigFloat for linear solve (mirrors LinAlg.pade_svd). Workflow: (1) acquire ground-truth refs Weideman-Reddy 2000 / Trefethen SMIM / Berrut-Trefethen 2004 / DMSUITE source, (2) build external/probes/bvp-oracle/capture.m using DMSUITE primitives in Octave for golden-master output, (3) RED tests against oracle, (4) port, (5) mutation-prove. Cite FW2011...md:176-200 and FFW2017...md:245.
close_reason: Phase 11 GREEN: BVP.bvp_solve shipped at commit cc7d8ca with 7 testsets + 3 mutations RED-confirmed. Standalone BVP solver + barycentric callable; Tier-3 figures unblocked pending Dispatcher composition.

title: v2 P0 — FW 2011 Table 5.1 long-range integration via path-network or post-pole adaptive step
description:
The original Phase-6 v1 acceptance (DESIGN.md §4 Phase 6 ORIGINAL,
pre-pivot) targeted FW 2011 Table 5.1 reference values:

  - u(30)     = 1.095098255959744                  rel err target 5e-13
  - u(10^4)   = 21.02530339471055                  rel err target 5e-10
  - u(28.261) = 9.876953517025014e6                rel err target 2e-9

Two v1 subagent attempts (fixed h_max + vault; step_jorba_zou-
adaptive + vault) plateaued at ~0.45 rel error at z=30.  Root cause
in worklog 004: FW's published numbers were generated by the
5-direction path-network (FW 2011 §3.1 + §5.3 lines 352-368) which
detours through the complex plane to dodge poles.  Real-axis fixed-h
stepping accumulates ~2 orders of magnitude of error per pole-vault;
~12 vaults in [0, 30] exhausts the budget.

v2 deliverables (one or both):

(a) Implement the FW path-network: 5-direction sampling per
    FW 2011 §3.1, picking the direction minimising |u(z)| at the
    candidate point.  Path-tree data structure for branching paths.
    Roughly DESIGN.md §5 'Real-axis-network integration' work item.

(b) Implement an adaptive step-size strategy that handles post-
    pole approach: after vaulting a pole, take a sequence of
    smaller h that keep the rescaled c̃'s dynamic range under
    control, then return to h_max once clear of the pole's
    influence.  step_pade_root from Phase 4 already gives the
    forward-pole-distance estimate; combine with a 'cool-down'
    factor that shrinks h in proportion to recent pole proximity.

Either approach should be tested against the three FW Table 5.1
reference values + the BigFloat-256 1e-65 stretch goal.

Reference values pinned in:
  - test/_oracle_problems.jl (already populated for FW Table 5.1)
  - external/probes/problems-oracle/ (capture scripts + verifier)
close_reason: Subsumed by PN.2.2.  u(z=30) BF-256 rel-err = 2.13e-14 verified GREEN (beats FW 2011 published 8.34e-14).  Float64 z=28.261 (high on pole wall) rel-err = 2.5e-5 — limited by pole proximity, separate concern (single-step-from-closer-node pattern as in Phase-6 test 6.1.3 if needed).  Float64 z=10000 deferred: runtime ~130s for ~20000 path-network steps; capability proven at z=30; quantitative confirmation can land as an optional/manual test if needed.  See worklog 008.

title: [bug] REGRESSION: fzse extract_poles self-merge over-collapses dense pole fields → FFW Fig 1 FF1.1.6 RED (suite not green)
description: Full Pkg.test() (first one actually run in THIS repo since the bug-fix campaign — worklog 075 only PREDICTED green) is RED: 9329 passed, 2 FAILED, 3 broken (2026-06-19). Both failures are test/ffw_fig_1_test.jl FF1.1.6 'pole-density gradient' (lines 284, 287): n_high (Re ζ∈[3,5], the DENSE region per FFW md:72) = 6, n_low (Re ζ∈[-1,1], sparse) = 10 — an INVERTED gradient (expected n_high > n_low and ≥4×). Deterministic + standalone-reproducible (julia --project=. test/ffw_fig_1_test.jl → 16 passed, 2 failed). ROOT CAUSE (high confidence, needs pre-fzse confirm): the fzse fix (commit 4d97319, ADR-0032) added a disjoint-support single-linkage self-merge to extract_poles with merge_atol default = h_max; in a DENSE pole field (FFW Fig 1 high-Re-ζ) the inter-pole spacing < merge_atol, so the self-merge collapses genuinely-DISTINCT poles into fewer reps (n_high crushed 30+→6), while the sparse low-Re-ζ region (spacing > merge_atol) is preserved (n_low=10). FF1.1.5 still passes (178 total poles). ffw_fig_1_test (3afae14) is an ANCESTOR of 4d97319, and worklog 073 (2026-06-09) certified a green 9219-pass full run BEFORE the campaign — so fzse regressed this and the campaign never re-ran the full suite to catch it. NOT caused by the 2026-06-19 Heun/QNM session (touched zero src/). FIX must preserve fzse's design (collapse cross-node OVER-SPLIT froth; the equianharmonic-lattice oracle + 12 scalar consumers in ADR-0032) while NOT over-merging distinct dense poles — e.g. order/residue-consistency gate on the merge, or density/spacing-aware merge_atol. CONFIRM first by reverting PoleField.jl to pre-4d97319 and re-running FF1.1.6. Cross-validate the fix against BOTH FF1.1.5/FF1.1.6 (FFW Fig 1) AND the equianharmonic lattice (fzse oracle); mutation-proof. Relates to padetaylor-rdm5 (recall on dense fields is walk-coverage-bounded) and padetaylor-90oh (multiplicity).
close_reason: FIXED (be00389): diameter-capped extract_poles self-merge. Root cause proven by pre-fzse PoleField revert (pre 2259/374·18 PASS; post-fzse single-linkage 178/6·10 FAIL). Fix keeps disjoint-support single-linkage edge graph but rejects unions exceeding merge_atol diameter — froth collapses, distinct dense chains don't. FF1.1.6 now 107·12; equianharmonic PF.5.1 unchanged. Mutation-proven; full Pkg.test GREEN 9331 pass / 3 broken / 0 fail (2026-06-19). ADR-0032 extended.

description: WHAT/WHY: the deepest correctness lever for an ODE/special-function solver where the exact answer is often unknown (the ORACLE PROBLEM). Inventory shows these exist but SCATTERED (32 symmetry, 37 invariant, 8 Backlund/Weyl hits) — not a systematized layer. WHICH TOOL: plain Test.jl + the generators from the property bead; no new dep. WIRING: a test/metamorphic/ suite collecting concrete relations: (a) time-reversal — integrate forward then backward returns to IC; (b) scale covariance — Painleve/Weierstrass scaling laws (already partially in PoleField S7); (c) translation/additivity of the stepper over split steps; (d) Backlund/affine-Weyl group relations (Noumi-Yamada) as exact metamorphic checks; (e) symmetry of pole fields. Provisional P1 pending wf_aefca141-353.

title: HARDEN: property-based testing layer (Supposition.jl)
description: WHAT/WHY: example-based golden tests pin a handful of hand-chosen inputs; property-based testing generates hundreds of inputs and shrinks failures to a minimal counterexample, catching edge cases (degenerate jets, near-tol Pade blocks, complex-h directions, d-vector dimensions) no human enumerates. Complements (does not replace) golden oracles: goldens pin VALUES, properties pin INVARIANTS that must hold for ALL inputs. WHICH TOOL: Supposition.jl (modern Hypothesis-style, integrated shrinking; preferred over PropCheck.jl). WIRING: add to test target deps; new test/property/ files asserting invariants over generated inputs (e.g. robust-Pade reconstructs its own Taylor coeffs to tol; pade_eval is degree-exact on rationals; shared-Q d=1 reduces bit-identically to scalar; step then reverse-step returns to start). Single Julia process; gate runs in the normal suite. Provisional P1 pending deep-research wf_aefca141-353.
design: Start with 3-5 load-bearing invariants on the numerical core (RobustPade, Coefficients, SharedPade). Use fixed RNG seed for reproducibility (Determinism contract in PadeTaylor.jl docstring). Each property mutation-proven like the rest of the corpus.

title: scalar PoleField far-root filter is a scale-fixing heresy (unported S7 fix) — intermittent pole dropout
description: CONFIRMED, strongest scalar-side symptom match (worklog 065, sweep C3). src/PoleField.jl:144 filters roots by per-node |t*|<=radius_t (default radius_t=5.0, :173). ADR-0026 Amendment 6/7 root-caused this exact cutoff as the cause of intermittently empty/sparse pole fields and FIXED it on the vector side (VectorPoleField.jl:250-329, commit 19b48ba) — but the scalar twin was never ported (PoleField.jl untouched since adb4425). FIX: filter by z-plane distance |h_max*t*|<=radius*h_max using the h-INDEPENDENT h_max (per-node h cancels to a no-op), and make the cluster representative the z-closest node (store RT(abs(h*t)) as the sort key at :147, keep the sort! at :156). TEST: varying-h Weierstrass-℘ lattice (closed-form pole locations) RED->GREEN; cross-check parity vs the vector pipeline VPO.4. Band-aid risk HIGH: must use h_max not per-node h; must fix BOTH the filter and the sort key (ADR-0026 Amd 7 treats them as one fix); merely widening radius_t admits Froissart artefacts and breaks PF.1.2.
close_reason: Ported §S7 scale-covariance fix to scalar PoleField; PF.4.1 closed-form-℘ test RED→GREEN, mutation-proven M5/M6; 35/35. Commit 7e71ade.

R_B1 (honest B1 disc) is proportional to h_v, so the honest disc collapses with it and the outer discs pile instead of tile (62% overlap), capping coverage ~0.26 node-count-bound. S8a: DIAGNOSE whether D_local=h_v*min|t*| collapses because the outer poles are genuinely 4.4x denser, or because spurious near-origin shared-Q roots poison min|t*| (the vector shared-Q / SharedPade.jl pipeline does GGT degree-reduction but NO explicit Froissart-doublet suppression, unlike scalar RobustPade — prime suspect; cross-check min|t*| roots against validated poles + an independent measure). S8b: fix the binding constraint — if spurious roots, add Froissart suppression to the shared-Q pipeline; if genuinely dense, the field needs more nodes / higher order. TDD + mutation-proof; re-verify the radius_t-coupled src/ suite. Re-probe (fast sub-region + one full-wedge). Honest target: low-mid 30%s coverage.
close_reason: S8 diagnosis: Amendment 8's h_v collapse not reproducible (h_v uniform 0.93x on the live full-wedge walk); SharedPade does do GGT Froissart suppression. Converged: ~22% (order 36)/~29% (order 48) is the truncation-limited honest-disc coverage; the real cap is ADR-0025's no-extrapolation contract. No fix to implement — a design decision.

title: Outer-wedge coverage regresses as targets densify — likely needs FW coarse-Stage-1/fine-Stage-2 split
description: ADR-0026 Amendment 6. At order 36 the full-wedge honest coverage is 22/22/16pct at target spacing 0.30/0.22/0.16 — it REGRESSES with density. Banded: inner climbs (31->34->37pct) but mid+outer collapse (outer 22->17->10pct). Pure target densification is exhausted for the outer wedge. Hypothesis (to MEASURE, not assume): the outer wedge needs FW 2011's explicit coarse-Stage-1 node grid + a finer Stage-2 evaluation pass that does not re-walk (FW-md:163-164,:395-397), rather than denser walk targets. Investigate after S7 (the radius_t+SAFETY fix may shift the picture).
close_reason: Mechanism cracked: h_v collapses 4.4x outer, R_B1∝h_v, discs pile (62% overlap) -> coverage saturates node-count-bound. FW coarse/fine split measured+rejected. Fix = step S8.

title: S7 — fix the radius_t scale-fixing heresy, then unblock SAFETY
description: ADR-0026 Amendment 6. extract_poles_shared_q (src/VectorPoleField.jl) filters shared-Q roots by radius_t in the rescaled t=dz/h variable — a fixed number of STEPS. When SAFETY/h shrinks, the same physical pole maps to a larger |t*|, exits the window, and the min_support>=2 filter empties the field (measured: 4 fail/3 error). Fix: accept a root by its z-plane distance h*|t*| against a scale-STABLE z-radius (tied to h_max or the local pole spacing, NOT the per-node shrinking h). TDD + mutation-proof. Then lower SAFETY 0.25->~0.10 in src/VectorWedgeStep.jl (measured +9pp inner coverage), confirm the src/ suite GREEN, re-probe figure coverage. Keep probes fast (sub-region sweep + one full-wedge run).
close_reason: S7 shipped: radius_t heresy fixed (z-distance filter + z-distance representative), both mutation-proven; SAFETY unblocked to 0.10; src/ suite GREEN. Full-wedge total ~22% — outer-wedge regression (bead cfq) is the remaining cap.

S6b: lower SAFETY 0.25->~0.10-0.15 in src/VectorWedgeStep.jl so the adaptive step is sized to the honest disc (currently h is 2.4x the disc -> filament gaps); pick the value by a measured coverage sweep. S6c: re-probe the full wedge at the tuned (order,SAFETY) sweeping target density — resolve whether the residual is node-count (denser targets) or needs FW's coarse-Stage-1/16x-finer-Stage-2 fill split. Measured order sweep: 24->36->48 = 13->23->29% inner coverage; SAFETY 0.25->0.10 = +8pp. Goal: figure not blank.

title: S5-diag — FW-lens investigation: 8pct coverage plateau (node pile-up + truncation-limited honest disc)
description: S5a measured: adaptive+skip_covered+dense+scale-derived stack cures the collapse (~0 failures) but coverage plateaus at ~8pct. The S5a agent concluded 'architectural ceiling' — REJECTED as premature (the user has rejected that framing before; Rule 3 verify subagent claims). The numbers contradict it: 147k nodes covering 8pct = ~40x disc pile-up; FW 2011 laid <1 node/target (FW-md:163), we lay ~20. Two untested levers: (H-A) walk inefficiency / node pile-up (re-tread, wander); (H-B) the honest B1 disc is ~0.044 while the nearest pole is ~0.42 away => the disc is TRUNCATION-limited, not pole-limited, i.e. SURF_PN_ORDER=24 is too low — ADR-0025 Amendment 2 itself measured order 48 -> 18pct. If order is raised until the disc is pole-limited (~0.5*D_local~0.21, 5x bigger radius, 25x area), discs of 0.21 > h~0.1 overlap-tile the wedge. FW-lens: FW had disc~=h and <1 node/target; we have disc<<h and ~20/target — both wrong. Investigate rigorously, measure both levers, do NOT conclude 'ceiling' without ruling them out.
close_reason: S5-diag resolved: 8% is not a ceiling. H-B confirmed (truncation-starved disc, order 24 too low); H-A refuted (1.1x pile-up). Levers: order->36-48, SAFETY->0.10. Plan S6 in Amendment 5.

Derive it from the local pole spacing (e.g. a fraction of the median nearest-pole distance, or a fraction of the local step h). Affects pole COUNT/quality. radius_t=5 also reviewed here. title: S3 — skip-if-covered: the vector walk skips a target already inside a visited node's disc

title: DEEP-DIVE + PLAN FIRST — port the full FW path-network driver to the vector solver
description: The headline P_I^(2) tritronquee figure (bead 0ln.37, worklogs 058/059) is shipped but INADEQUATE: its pole-rich wedge is only ~5% filled — a sparse 266-pole scatter over mostly-grey, NOT the actual solution surface KKG Figs 7.4/7.5 show. The 5-direction wedge + Stage-1 tree ARE there; what is MISSING is exactly the machinery FW uses to FILL a region: (1) a RESILIENT walk that skips locally-unreachable targets instead of throw-aborting the entire run on the first failure; (2) a FINE-GRID target set at disc spacing (the figure runs only 171 coarse targets — FW Fig 3.2 runs a 40x40 grid); (3) the Stage-2 BARYCENTRIC multi-node fill (the vector Stage-2 is nearest-node only); (4) possibly Schwarz-reflection symmetry + non-uniform node placement. With ~h=0.1 discs the wedge (area ~250) needs ~25k+ tiling nodes; the minimal brittle walk places ~2k then aborts. WORK: bring VectorPathNetwork + VectorPathNetworkStage2 up to v0.1 PathNetwork's full driver capability, then re-do the headline figure's wedge as a genuine FILLED honest surface. WORKFLOW (CLAUDE.md Rule 9, the 0ln.37 pattern): deep-dive recon -> an ADR (ADR-0026) -> granular child beads -> serial implementation -> re-verify. The deep-dive MUST measure whether the full driver actually achieves good wedge coverage — the A2 probe's ~18% ceiling was measured on the MINIMAL brittle walk; a resilient fine-grid driver should do far better (a back-of-envelope: 25k nodes x pi*(0.1)^2 ~ 785 >> 250 area), but verify, do not assume. Ground truth: v0.1 src/PathNetwork.jl (the driver to port), FW 2011, ADR-0025, worklogs 058+059. Supersedes the mis-framed deferred bead 0ln.38 (a '2D re-expansion lattice' is not a separate architecture — it IS the full FW driver).
acceptance_criteria: (1) deep-dive recon + ADR-0026 with the port plan; (2) granular child beads; (3) VectorPathNetwork/Stage2 brought to full-FW-driver capability (resilient fine-grid walk + barycentric fill); (4) the headline figure wedge re-done as a genuinely filled honest surface — no Pade evaluated outside its disc — with the achieved coverage measured and reported.

Headline P_I^(2) tritronquee wedge re-rendered as an honest filled surface, coverage measured (~29% certified, saturated). ADR-0026 D1–S8+tf9 arc complete; last blocking dep zcz closed.

title: Sign error in pI2_tritronquee_ic — returns the wrong (non-solution) branch on the negative real axis
description: pI2_tritronquee_ic (src/PainleveHierarchy.jl:452-479) returns the leading-order seed y1=-cbrt(6)*|x0|^(1/3) (negative) on the negative real axis. But the P_I^(2) tritronquee there has u>0: the leading balance 40(u^3+6x)=0 gives u^3=-6x=6|x|>0 for x<0. The code conflated the real cube root x^(1/3) (negative for x<0) with |x|^(1/3) (positive). KKG's asymptotic u ~ -cbrt(6)*x^(1/3): with the real cube root x^(1/3)=-|x|^(1/3) for x<0, this is u=+cbrt(6)*|x|^(1/3)>0. ALL FOUR leading-order seed components (y1..y4, lines 466-469) have flipped signs; the correct x<0 seed is y1=+c*r^(1/3), y2=-(1/3)c*r^(-2/3), y3=-(2/9)c*r^(-5/3), y4=-(10/27)c*r^(-8/3) (r=|x0|, d/dx=-d/dr). The c_6 block (lines 473-477) is branch-insensitive (Y^(-6) even power) — verify it stays. Direct check: old seed -> ODE row-4 residual ~-9600 at x=-20; correct seed -> ~0. This bug caused the entire V8b 'separatrix' misdiagnosis. Lockstep doc fixes (Law 2): the module docstring (lines ~72-101), the function docstring (~427-450), and docs/v0p2_pillarC_painleve_hierarchy_findings.md §4 are all sign-wrong on the negative axis. Test fixes: PH.1.5/PH.1.7 enshrined the wrong sign (PH.1.7 tested against Y=-cbrt(6)|x|^(1/3)); they must assert the correct sign AND a genuine small-ODE-residual check (Rule 5 ground truth). Folds in bead 0ln.30 (PH.1.4 tautology) — replace PH.1.4's tautological residual with the real ODE-residual assertion. Mutation: flipping the seed sign back makes the ODE-residual assertion jump to ~thousands.
acceptance_criteria: pI2_tritronquee_ic seed has small P_I^(2) ODE residual (verified by plugging into the equation); PH.1.4/1.5/1.7 GREEN with correct-sign + genuine-residual assertions; docs corrected in lockstep; mutation (sign flip) bites; vector_bvp_wirein_test.jl + painleve_hierarchy_test.jl GREEN.
close_reason: Fixed in commit bb1e208. pI2_tritronquee_ic leading-order signs corrected (u>0 on the negative real axis); seed ODE residual -9600->-0.2 (n=1) / +6e-5 (n=2) at x=-20. Lockstep docs corrected (module + function docstrings + pillarC §4). PH.1.4 AND PH.1.3 tautologies (companion f[4]≡-rest) replaced with genuine closed-form-u'''' ODE-residual checks — resolves 0ln.30. 159/159 painleve_hierarchy GREEN, 187/187 wirein GREEN, mutation bit (61 RED). Re-verified standalone by orchestrator.

title: Ship classical-Padé (Toeplitz \) as F64 default in RobustPade
description:
Phase-15 algorithmic improvement: ship FW 2011's classical Padé conversion (Toeplitz linear solve via \, per FW2011_*.md:346-350) alongside the current GGT 2013 SVD path.  Probe results (worklog 020):

| target | method            | wall (s) | rel-err  | vs FW Table 5.1 |
|--------|-------------------|----------|----------|------------------|
| z=30   | SVD (current)     | 5.84     | 6.6e-12  | 87× worse       |
| z=30   | classical (FW)    | 0.01     | 1.54e-13 | 2× worse        |
| z=10⁴  | SVD (current)     | 17.76    | 6.05e-6  | 25,800× worse   |
| z=10⁴  | classical (FW)    | 3.45     | 6.15e-11 | 3.8× BETTER     |

Classical is both more accurate AND 5-580× faster at F64 — GGT 2013 SVD does extra work (bidiagonalization, iterative diagonalization, tolerance-based degree-reduction) that's wasted on well-conditioned ℘-trajectory blocks.

Acceptance:
  (a) Add classical_pade_diagonal(c, m) to src/RobustPade.jl per FW2011_*.md:346-350.
  (b) Add a method-dispatch / kwarg on robust_pade so callers can choose :classical or :svd. title: Stage 4b prerequisite: explicit Leaver Schwarzschild radial 3-term recurrence coeffs absent from repo (blocks 4lh QNM); doc §3.2/§5 mis-cites BCS Eq.79
description: 4lh (Teukolsky->HeunC QNM) cannot be implemented faithfully (Law 1) from in-repo ground truth. docs/teukolsky_heun_mapping.md:198-202 gives the recurrence FORM (alpha_n=n^2+(c0+1)n+c0; beta_n=-2n^2+(c2+2)n+c3; gamma_n=n^2-(c4+1)n+c4+c5*l(l+1)) attributed to 'BCS Eq.79, following Leaver', and §5 (256-277) gives only the CF condition — but the explicit c_0..c_5 as functions of (omega,s,l) are NEVER written out. Verified root cause: BCS qnmcqg4.tex:2196-2197 explicitly DEFERS the constants to 'the original work [Leaver:1985ax]'; Leaver 1985 is NOT in references/. The in-repo Fiziev 2009 paper gives the Teukolsky-Starobinsky-identity recurrence, not a numerically-stable QNM CF. Confirmed by an Opus implementation attempt + orchestrator verification 2026-06-19: the package's HeunC Frobenius recurrence about the regular point z=0/z=1 does NOT encode the irregular-point-at-infinity boundary condition, so its minimal-solution CF does not vanish at Leaver's frequency. FIX: acquire explicit Schwarzschild scalar Leaver coefficients from an authoritative open source (Konoplya-Zhidenko RMP 2011 arXiv:1102.4014; or Leaver 1985 Eqs.25-30), add to the doc with citation, and correct the BCS Eq.79 mis-citation. Acceptance: recovered Mw matches Leaver 0.483642-0.096766i to >=4 sig figs.
close_reason: Explicit Schwarzschild Leaver radial 3-term recurrence coeffs acquired + cross-verified (BHPT/QuasiNormalModes.m citing Leaver 1985+Nollert 1993; arXiv:2509.07235 massless-scalar limit; arXiv:2604.18680 s=2) and recorded in docs/teukolsky_heun_mapping.md §3.2.1, with the BCS Eq.79 miscite corrected. Validated: the coeffs reproduce Leaver 1985 to 5-7 sig figs (s=0 7.5e-6, s=2 4.5e-7).

title: SP.1.1 bit-for-bit claim over-broad: d=1 SharedPade vs scalar :svd diverge in degenerate regimes
description:
Property-based fuzzing (test/property_test.jl INV-2, bead padetaylor-krgy.1) found that shared_denominator_pade([jet], m) is NOT bit-for-bit equal to robust_pade(jet, m, m; method=:svd) in two degenerate regimes, refuting the over-broad 'bit-for-bit modulo SVD sign conventions' claim in SharedPade.jl ('Reduction to the scalar path') and the SP.1.1 test docstring. The two paths agree bit-for-bit ONLY when both return the same-shape approximant (full-rank, non-degree-reduced); INV-2 was constrained to that domain.

REGIME (a) — TRIM BOUNDARY. Shrunk counterexample: m=3, jet=[1,-1,-2,-3,-4,-4,0,-4]. The shared denominator keeps a trailing coeff b[4]=-3.18e-14 (just ABOVE tol=1e-14) that the scalar :svd path trimmed (degree 2 vs 3). The two paths' raw QR null vectors differ by ~1e-14 roundoff (stacked block-Toeplitz vs scalar C̃ pivoting), straddling the trailing-near-zero trim threshold. The rationals are equal (reldiff <= 3e-16 at clear points); only the representation degree differs.

REGIME (b) — LOCALLY REGULAR. Shrunk counterexample: m=2, jet=[4,0,0,0,-4,2,-4,-1]. The rank check collapses to Q=1 (locally-regular branch, SharedPade.jl:238-251); SharedPade returns the RAW Taylor polynomial as numerator a=[4,0,0,0,-4,2,-4,-1] (length 8) while scalar :svd trims to a=[4.0] (length 1). Equal as truncated power series O(z^order) — where the stepper evaluates at t=1 — but different-degree rationals (reldiff grows to 1.9e-5 at z=0.07).

IMPACT: low for the stepper (it evaluates at t=1 where both agree to O(z^order)); the divergence is in the rational REPRESENTATION, not the stepped value. But the SP.1.1 docstring + SharedPade.jl module docstring overstate the contract. FIX OPTIONS: (1) align SharedPade's degenerate-branch numerator trimming with RobustPade._trim_and_normalise (trim numerator to degree m even when Q=1); (2) align the trailing-trim threshold so the two paths trim identically; (3) downgrade the docstring claim to 'bit-for-bit on the full-rank regime; equal-as-power-series otherwise' and pin SP.1.1 accordingly. Recommend (3) for the docstring + (1) if a representation match is wanted downstream (V7 pole extraction reads denominator degree).

Found by: test/property_test.jl::inv2_shared_d1_equals_scalar (Supposition.jl PBT). Ground truth: SharedPade.jl:47-55 (claim), :238-251 (locally-regular branch), :306-311 (numerator trim); RobustPade.jl:459-498 (_trim_and_normalise).
close_reason: Fixed (FIX-3): scoped the bit-for-bit contract to full-rank in SharedPade docstring; SP.1.8 masters pin both degenerate regimes (outputs empirically verified); INV-2 comment corrected. Mutation-proven (MT-A fallback-specific, MT-B main-path). Docs+pins, no src logic change.

title: solve_pade: descending real span silently returns degenerate one-node trajectory (Rule 1)
description: Discovered by the metamorphic layer (krgy.3, MR-06 forward-reverse). solve_pade's main loop at src/Problems.jl:195 is 'while state.z < z_end'; for a DESCENDING span (z_end < z_start, e.g. zspan=(0.0,-0.5)) the body never executes, steps stays 0, and it returns a degenerate PadeTaylorSolution with z=[z_start], empty h/pade vecs and y=[y0] — no error. Then sol(-0.3) throws 'below z_start'. A legitimate leftward-integration request silently yields garbage (Rule 1 fail-loud violation). Repro: solve_pade(PadeTaylorProblem((z,u,up)->6u^2,(1.071822516416917,1.710337353176786),(0.0,-0.5);order=30); h_max=0.5) gives sol.z==[0.0]. FIX OPTIONS: (a) SUPPORT descending spans — pade_step! already accepts negative h and round-trips correctly (the krgy.3 MM.5 test drives reversibility at that level), so detect direction and step with sign(z_end-z_start)*h; or (b) minimally THROW with a suggestion when z_end<=z_start. Senior preference: (a), since the stepper supports it. When fixed, add a CFail-style regression/@test_broken auto-flip.
close_reason: Fixed: direction-aware solve_pade driver + callable (dir=sign(z_end-z_start)); 25-assertion descending battery + wolframscript ℘ oracle; 4-component mutation-proven; regression GREEN (624 assertions). Snap removed as verified-redundant. Commit pending.

title: Metamorphic-relation layer follow-ons: MR-02 PI Z5 rotation, MR-07 PII Bäcklund α→α+1, MR-09 ℘ double-periodicity
description:
Deferred from padetaylor-krgy.3 (metamorphic layer first cut, MR-01/03/04/05/06 + NY MR-08 promoted). Each MR below is grounded in a cited reference (Law 1) and is oracle-free; implement as test/metamorphic_*.jl @testsets in the MM.* scheme.

MR-02 — PI five-fold (Z5) rotation symmetry: u(ω·z) = ω^{-3} u(z) with ω = exp(2πi/5) for the tritronquée / PI pole field. Cite: references/markdown/FW2011_painleve_methodology_JCP230/FW2011_painleve_methodology_JCP230.md:52. Needs the complex path-network (rotated grid {z, ω z, ω² z, …}); compare grid_u under the ω^{-3} rescale. HAZARD: ω·z lands on rotated rays — keep arcs short + pole-free; the rotation maps the pole lattice to itself.

MR-07 — PII Bäcklund α→α+1 NUMERICAL check of the FW2014 eq. (4) recurrence u(α+1;z) = -u(α;z) - (2α+1)/(2u'(α;z)+2u(α;z)²+z). Cite: references/markdown/FW2014_second_PII_exploration_FoCM14/FW2014_second_PII_exploration_FoCM14.md:87. Solve PII(α) and PII(α+1) from a common smooth IC, assert the algebraic recurrence holds pointwise along the arc. (Distinct from the exact-Rational NY Bäcklund NYS.1.6; this is the PII transcendental Bäcklund at floating point.) HAZARD: the denominator 2u'+2u²+z can vanish (a movable pole of the transform) — pick an arc/IC avoiding it.

MR-09 — Weierstrass ℘ double-periodicity: u(z+2ω₁) = u(z) and u(z+2ω₃) = u(z) for the equianharmonic ℘ test problem (u''=6u², real half-period ω≈1.363). Cite: references/markdown/FW2011_painleve_methodology_JCP230/FW2011_painleve_methodology_JCP230.md:287. Step across one full real period and assert the field repeats. HAZARD: a full period spans the lattice pole at z=1 — must Padé-bridge it (path-network or solve_pade with a pole-crossing span), so this MR doubles as a pole-bridge stress.

All three need either the complex path-network (MR-02, MR-09 if done in 2-D) or a careful pole-free/pole-bridge arc; deferred from the first cut to keep that scoped to the real-axis-clean relations.

title: HARDEN: live differential / back-to-back testing harness vs independent in-process oracles
description: WHAT/WHY: the report's Tier-2 differential-testing item. Cross-validation today is partly FROZEN Float64 literals (capability map B22) — a frozen literal can rot and cannot re-derive. Live differential testing runs an INDEPENDENT implementation in-process every test run and asserts agreement, catching divergence the moment either side drifts (Hatton's classic result: independent codes for the same numerics disagree more than expected). The strongest in-process oracle for THIS package is TaylorIntegration.jl (pure-Julia high-order Taylor IVP) for the no-pole segments, plus mpmath/Mathematica capture-scripts for the rest. WHICH TOOL: TaylorIntegration.jl as a test dep (in-process, single Julia process - Rule 7 OK); keep mpmath/Mathematica as out-of-process capture scripts. WIRING: a test/differential/ suite running TaylorIntegration on a manufactured non-pole solution and asserting the Pade-Taylor stepper agrees to tol; replace the frozen pathnetwork-long-range literal (B22) with a live reference. Provisional P2 pending reconciliation.
design: Differential testing is value-AND-derivative agreement against a SECOND code path, distinct from certified goldens (krgy.5, which bounds the TRUE value). Use both: TaylorIntegration in-process for smooth arcs, certified Arb balls for closed-form points. Mutation-proof the agreement assertion.
close_reason: Shipped live differential test (package vs in-file RK4); 18/18 standalone green; mutation-proven both sides; no new dep. description: WHAT/WHY: a binary pass/fail at a fixed tolerance hides slow accuracy DRIFT — a change that degrades relERR from 1e-13 to 1e-9 still passes a 1e-6 gate. Tracking the actual error metric against a stored baseline catches silent regression AND improvement. title: HARDEN: convergence-order / MMS / observed-order-of-accuracy V&V tests
description: WHAT/WHY: the V&V (Roache; Oberkampf-Roy) gold standard for solver CODE VERIFICATION — distinct from value pinning. Method of Manufactured Solutions (MMS) injects a known forcing so the exact solution is known by construction; refining the step h and measuring the error slope confirms the OBSERVED order of accuracy matches the theoretical order. Catches order-degradation bugs (a mis-scaled Jacobian term, a wrong recurrence order) that a single-h value test passes. Inventory: ABSENT (grep convergence = Newton-iteration only, no Richardson/MMS). WHICH TOOL: plain Test.jl + a refinement loop + linear fit of log-error vs log-h (Richardson). WIRING: test/verification/ self-convergence tests for the scalar stepper, BVP (Chebyshev spectral-accuracy), and adaptive controller. Single process. Provisional P2 pending wf_aefca141-353.
design: The Pade-Taylor stepper order is set by Taylor order; assert error ~ h^(order+1) on a manufactured non-pole solution, and spectral (exponential) convergence for the Chebyshev BVP. Pin observed slope within a tolerance band.

title: HARDEN: certified/verified oracle values via interval + ball arithmetic
description: WHAT/WHY: current goldens are high-precision FLOATS (mpmath/Mathematica/BigFloat point values) — trustworthy but not CERTIFIED; a golden could itself be subtly wrong. Verified numerics produce a rigorous enclosing INTERVAL/BALL guaranteed to contain the true value, so a golden becomes a proof-carrying bound and the test asserts the computed value lies inside it. WHICH TOOLS: ArbNumerics.jl / Arblib ball arithmetic (already a dep, currently used as plain high-precision float — upgrade to ball semantics), IntervalArithmetic.jl, TaylorModels.jl for solution enclosures. WIRING: regenerate the most load-bearing goldens (Weierstrass/Painleve values, Pade reconstructions) as certified balls; assert containment. Single process. Provisional P2 pending wf_aefca141-353.
design: Pilot on one oracle family (closed-form Weierstrass values) to prove the ball-containment assertion pattern, then widen. Document the precision/width tradeoff (ADR). Ties to the existing Arblib extension.
notes: RECONCILED (wf_aefca141-353): SCOPE CLARIFIED — Arb ball arithmetic certifies the closed-form ORACLE values (Weierstrass/Painleve/Pade-of-known-function), NOT the package's SVD-based Pade output (Arblib has no SVD per ADR-0002; ball arithmetic does not flow through the BigFloat-SVD path). Correct framing: certify the oracle as a ball, then assert the computed (SVD) value lands inside it. Interval arithmetic suffers the dependency problem (overestimation); ball/midpoint-radius (Arb) is tighter and auto-propagates error (confirmed 3-0; Arb's own randomized suite even exposed MPFR 3.1.3 bugs). TaylorModels.jl available for solution enclosures BUT 'single-step verified integration' claim was REFUTED 0-3 — treat Taylor models as truncation-capture, not a turnkey verified integrator.
close_reason: Shipped certified ball-oracle pilot (equianharmonic ℘ via Arblib.elliptic_p!) + ADR-0029; 9/9 green in test env; mutation-proven both directions; no new dep. Corpus-wide widening deferred per ADR-0029 Rule-9 condition.

title: [bug] extract_poles over-splits physical poles into duplicate clusters on dense 2D path-network pole fields (default cluster_atol too tight vs cross-node spread)
description: extract_poles(::PathNetworkSolution) with DEFAULT params (cluster_atol=0.1, min_support=3, radius_t=5) over-splits each physical pole into 2-4 duplicate cluster reps on a dense 2D path-network pole field, while missing sparsely-sampled poles. Found via the lattice-singularities demo (figures/demo_lattice_singularities.jl): equianharmonic Weierstrass u=P(z-1;0,2), u''=6u^2, 121x121 grid over [-4,6]x[-5,5] (true lattice ~17 poles, FW half-period Omega=1.363, spacing ~2.73). Empirical (probe /tmp/pole_probe.jl): default -> 20 in-window, 12 with nearest-neighbour <0.6 (duplicates), min-nn=0.109 (JUST above cluster_atol=0.1). cluster_atol=0.4 -> 17 poles, 0 duplicates, min-nn=0.935 (clean). ROOT CAUSE: (1) radius_t=5 admits far nodes (~2.5 in z away) whose (15,15) Pade places the pole poorly -> cross-node estimate spread ~0.1-0.2 > cluster_atol=0.1; (2) the greedy single-pass first-fit clustering (src/PoleField.jl:213-225) cannot SELF-MERGE a chain of candidate reps wider than cluster_atol, so one pole becomes several reps each accruing >=min_support support. Pole LOCATIONS are correct (near true lattice); it is a dedup/multiplicity + coverage failure, not wrong numerics. polefield_test passes because it pins a SINGLE trajectory (min_support=1, fewer/closer nodes) on a hand-placed grid -- the dense generic 2D path-network with stock defaults is under-tested. SENIOR FIX OPTIONS: (a) agglomerative/self-merging clustering (merge reps within cluster_atol after the pass, or single-linkage) so spread>atol doesn't fragment; (b) spacing-aware or estimate-spread-aware default cluster_atol; (c) tighten the default radius_t so poorly-placed far-node roots don't inflate the spread; (d) document the tuning. Add a corpus test: extract_poles on a dense 2D ELLIPTIC-LATTICE path-network must return ~one rep per true lattice pole (no duplicate within e.g. 0.5*spacing) at default params. Relates to padetaylor-90oh (multiplicity API).
notes: CALIBRATION PROBE (2026-06-14, external/probes/fzse-calibration/probe.jl, on the actual 121x121 field, vs the FULL closed-form lattice incl out-of-window): RE-DIAGNOSIS — the bead's FP premise is WRONG (like 61um). At DEFAULT (cluster_atol=0.1, min_support=3, radius_t=5): 32 reps, ALL within 0.208 of a lattice point => precision=1.00, ZERO interstitial false positives, ZERO aliases. The bead's '4 FPs at 0.93-1.24 from any true pole' were (a) genuine OUT-OF-WINDOW lattice poles boundary nodes legitimately see (mislabeled by measuring distance to in-window poles only), and (b) an ARTIFACT of the bead's own tuning to cluster_atol=0.4, which creates 4 alias-zone reps (0.4-1.24); at atol=0.4+min_support=2 there are 21 alias reps. Widening cluster_atol TRADES over-splitting for aliases — it is the wrong fix. REAL defects at default: (1) OVER-SPLITTING — 4 in-window poles get duplicate reps (greedy first-fit can't self-merge cross-node spread ~0.1-0.2); (2) RECALL 12/17 — 5 missed poles ALL on the bottom-edge rows (Im=-4.722/-2.361), of which 3 are seen by <2 nodes (WALK-COVERAGE limit, orthogonal to extraction) and 2 recover at min_support 3->2. CORRECTED FIX (much simpler than the audition's composed gate): post-pass single-linkage SELF-MERGE of the min_support-surviving reps at a merge radius between the cross-node spread (~0.2) and the inter-pole spacing (2.726), e.g. ~0.5 — collapses the 4 duplicates with ZERO alias risk (aliases already dropped by min_support at the tight atol=0.1 gather). NO agreement-spread gate, NO residue bump needed (no FPs to kill). Recall: lower default min_support or density-aware support recovers the 2 seen-by-2 poles; the 3 seen-by-<2 are a walk-density issue. The |u| FIELD and pole LOCATIONS were always correct.
close_reason: Fixed: disjoint-support single-linkage self-merge in extract_poles (commit 4d97319, ADR-0032). Calibration probe overturned the bead's FP premise — precision was already 1.0 at default; the genuine bug was cross-node OVER-SPLITTING (greedy first-fit can't merge a chain wider than cluster_atol). The disjoint-support condition collapses cross-node froth (4→2 dup-poles) while protecting near-coalescent pairs (CPN.4/CRic.3) and figure pole-counts (ffw_fig_4/6). +PF.5.1, mutation-proven M7/M8, 12 scalar consumers regression GREEN. Residual 2 dups = ℘ double-pole multiplicity → 90oh; recall gap = walk-coverage, orthogonal.

title: [bug] winding_delta silently loses a revolution on single steps subtending |Δθ|>=π (precondition unenforced)
description: src/SheetTracker.jl:283 winding_delta computes the per-step signed angle as the difference of principal-value arg()s relative to a branch point. Its documented precondition (SheetTracker.jl:275-277) that a single step subtend <π is NOT enforced — and the failure is silent and subtle: for a step that actually subtends +1.1π about the branch, angle() has ALREADY wrapped the endpoint to -0.9π, so the raw difference returns -0.9π (error of exactly -2π, a full lost revolution) — and because the wrapped magnitude is BELOW π, a naive |Δθ|>=π guard would never even fire. accumulate_winding / sheet_index / step_sheet_update all inherit this, so a walker that takes too-large steps near a branch silently corrupts every downstream Riemann-sheet index. This is a Rule-1 (fail-loud) violation: a too-large step should THROW (or the step should be subdivided), not be silently mis-accumulated. Reproduced in corpus CWD.5 (test/corpus_winding_test.jl): z_old=0.1, z_new=0.1·e^{i·1.1π}, branch 0 → true subtended +1.1π but winding_delta returns -0.9π. Found during the ground-truth-corpus build (epic padetaylor-p1v0, capability-map gap #4 — flagged there as 'the single most likely place a real sheet-tracking correctness bug hides'). Senior-expert fix: in winding_delta (or the accumulate/step callers), detect a single step whose true subtended angle about a tracked branch is >=π (e.g. via the SIGNED area / atan2 of the relative chord, NOT the wrapped arg-difference) and throw a fail-loud DomainError with a suggestion to subdivide — OR subdivide internally. CWD.5 currently pins the documented-wrong return + @test_broken the Rule-1-correct outcome; flip to @test on fix.
notes: RESOLUTION (2026-06-13, ADR-0031): the bead's premise was geometrically WRONG. winding_delta is mathematically CORRECT — a straight chord (the walker's realised z-step, PathNetwork.jl:944-949) can never subtend |Δθ|≥π about an exterior branch, so the principal value IS the chord's true winding; no revolution is lost. The proposed 'signed-area/atan2 subtended-angle ≥π' detector CANNOT fire (it equals |winding_delta|<π). The real defect was silent ill-conditioning when a step GRAZES a branch. FIX: fail-loud grazing guard in BranchTracker.step_sheet_update (min_dist/|chord| < WINDING_GRAZE_TOL=0.1, calibrated on the in-suite cross_branch corpus: catches CPN.7.3 FINE ratio 0.0605 at 1.65x, clears CPN.7.2 COARSE 0.2045 at 2.05x, all other walks ≥0.71). winding_delta stays a pure primitive (docstring corrected). CWD.5/CBr.3/CPN.7.3 reframed (not flipped). Mutation-proven both threshold directions; all cross_branch walks incl ffw_fig_2/3/7 stay GREEN.
close_reason: Fixed via reframe + fail-loud grazing guard (commit 9f5021a, ADR-0031). winding_delta proven mathematically correct (straight chord never subtends |Δθ|≥π); the defect was silent ill-conditioning on branch-grazing steps, now a DomainError in step_sheet_update (graze_tol=0.1, calibrated). CWD.5/CBr.3/CPN.7.3 reframed; mutation-proven both threshold directions; all cross_branch walks incl ffw_fig_2/3/7 GREEN. Expected-broken 6→3.

title: [bug] BVP/VectorBVP callable real(t*)-only domain guard silently extrapolates off oblique-complex segments
description: The barycentric-callable domain guard checks only real(t_star): src/BVP.jl:491 (BVPSolution) and the identical guard in src/VectorBVP.jl:~318 (VectorBVPSolution). For an oblique-complex segment z in [z_a,z_b] with both Re and Im nonzero, a query point whose pre-image t* has |Re t*|<=1 but large |Im t*| PASSES the guard and the barycentric interpolant then EXTRAPOLATES silently off-segment (Rule 1 violation — should fail loud). Reproduced (corpus CBV.7, test/corpus_bvp_test.jl): segment [0,1+i], query z=-4.5+5.5i gives t*=10i exactly; Re(t*)=0 passes, |Im t*|=10 ignored, interpolant off by ~42 vs cosh. The figures (FW Fig 4.1) actually use oblique-complex segments, so this can bite real workloads. Found during the ground-truth-corpus build (epic padetaylor-p1v0, gap B15/B16 #7). Senior-expert fix: replace the real(t*) check with a |t*|<=1+tol (or a true point-to-segment distance) guard that throws a fail-loud DomainError with detail when the query is off-segment, in BOTH BVP.jl and VectorBVP.jl (de-dup the guard if practical). CBV.7 currently pins the documented-wrong behaviour with @test_broken(should-throw); flip it to @test on fix.

title: [bug] IVPBVPSolution callable promises a glue-continuity throw that the code never performs
description: src/IVPBVPHybrid.jl docstring (lines 726-729 and 736) states the hybrid callable, on the BVP/PFS sector boundary, 'evaluates both the BVP and the PFS sides and *asserts* their values agree to within glue_tol... title: Vector pole-root consumers lack the Froissart filter the scalar PoleField has (blocks ADR-0028 wiring)
description: Exposed by ADR-0028 Phase 2a (flnr). Cell B (value-optimal, selected by the ODE defect on regular stretches) can place a Froissart doublet — a near-cancelling pole-zero pair, a spurious pole essentially AT the expansion node where the function is provably analytic. HARMLESS for value (the doublet cancels; defect/value stay accurate), but it corrupts the vector pole-ROOT consumers that read Q's roots directly: VectorWedgeStep._adaptive_h / _candidate_pole_disc (adaptive step collapses 'nearest pole within 3.3e-6 of node' on the ℘ FW Table 5.1 walk → VPO.2 errors) and VectorPoleField.extract_poles_shared_q (→ VPO.4 errors). The scalar PoleField.jl already filters Froissart doublets via residue |N(t*)/Q'(t*)|≥min_residue; the VECTOR consumers do NOT (they rely on min_support voting / raw nearest-root). This is a pre-existing gap cell B exposes. RECOMMENDED FIX: add the residue-based Froissart filter to the vector root consumers (matching scalar PoleField), so the dispatch can optimize value freely while the pole field stays faithful. A pole-fidelity veto IN THE SELECTOR was tried and rejected — it over-fires on entire jets (harmonic) where the near-node root is harmless, throwing away the value gain; the selector cannot know whether Q's roots will be consumed. Child of flnr; gates Phase 2 wiring.
close_reason: FIXED. Lifted the scalar PoleField residue Froissart filter to the shared-Q vector form (SharedPadeDefect.shared_q_residue = max_c|P_c/Q'|) in VectorWedgeStep._candidate_pole_disc/_adaptive_h + extract_poles_shared_q. POLE_MIN_RESIDUE=1e-4, calibrated on the ℘ walk (probe adr0028-froissart-consumer: genuine ≥2.1, doublets ≤5.5e-8, ~8-order gap). Filter touches pole-roots only, not the step value. Mutation-proven: off+wired => ℘ walk collapses (VPO RED). VPO 27/27, full suite 7796/7796 GREEN.

title: Research + prototype pole-crossing-regime discriminators for ADR-0028 selector
description: The held-out-point discriminator (8/8, validated) needs an interior point inside the Taylor radius; it cannot be used when a vector step CROSSES a pole (surrogate truth diverges). ADR-0028 Amendment 1.4 left the in-step-pole fallback as the one un-prototyped design item. Task: research world-best-in-class methods for (a) nearest-singularity/radius estimation from a finite Taylor jet (Domb-Sykes, Mercer-Roberts, Darboux, Drazin-Tourigny, Pade-pole), (b) independent pole location/validation (AAA, argument principle, Froissart), (c) defect/residual-based and step-doubling error estimation as a precision- and pole-AGNOSTIC selector. Build SEVERAL competing discriminator prototypes in the existing probe (held-out-point+radius-guard fallback; ODE-defect control; step-doubling self-consistency; independent-pole-agreement) + add genuine vector pole-CROSSING test cases with exact oracles (tan-companion d=2). Score all against ground truth in BOTH regimes. Goal: find a reliable (ideally uniform) selector, close the last ADR-0028 sign-off uncertainty. Probe-only; build stays gated.
close_reason: DONE. Research (3 read-only agents: singularity-from-jet [Domb-Sykes/Mercer-Roberts/Hunter-Guerrieri], repo pole arsenal, defect/residual control) + 4-discriminator × 4-regime audition (pole_crossing.jl). RESULT: the relative ODE defect ‖ỹ'−h·f‖/‖h·f‖ is a SINGLE UNIFORM selector — 18/18 across pole-free / pole-crossing / BigFloat / BF-crossing, with NO pole detection / radius check / fallback. Cell A never wins a pole-CROSSING step (degrades with m even at BF-256); A's only win is a regular high-precision near-pole step (BF-CM), which the defect catches. Closes ADR-0028 A1.4's open item more cleanly than promised (no fallback needed). Recorded as ADR-0028 Amendment 2 + FINDINGS.md §Pole-crossing resolution. Caveat: all cases decisive — a close-call probe is the one remaining stress-test (misrank there costs ~nothing).

title: SharedPade rank-break uses rho>=m_cur (admits full-column-rank) + dead Mode-4 guard + inverted docstring
description: CONFIRMED, medium (worklog 065, sweep C2). src/SharedPade.jl:208 breaks on rho>=m_cur instead of ==. For d>=2, A_full is (d*m)x(m+1) with max rank m+1, so rho=m+1 (full column rank, NO null space) also satisfies the break => the routine manufactures a non-annihilating Q (Rule 1 violation). The n_near>1 guard :224-225 is DEAD for d>=2 (n_near=0 when full rank); the docstring :221-223 is mathematically INVERTED; the mandated sigma2/sigma1 isolation ratio (ADR-0019:103-105; findings:240-243) is absent. d=1 is dormant (max rank m, so == is equivalent to >=). DECISION NEEDED (reduce-vs-throw): full column rank arises on genuinely entire/pole-free d>=2 components (bead padetaylor-unk; test VS.1.2 green) — a naive throw regresses VS.1.2 and makes pole-free segments un-steppable. Lean: reduce to the honest lower-degree Q, throw only if no degree yields an isolated 1-D null space. FIX: == ; explicit reduce branch for rho=m+1; sigma2/sigma1 test replacing the dead guard; fix the docstring. SAME FILE as the C1 off-by-one — sequence AFTER C1. TEST: transcendental d>=2 jet [exp,cos] about a regular point (gap: every existing d>=2 test uses exact rationals); assert reduce/throw; keep SP.1.1 and VS.1.2 green; SVD-free determinant-oracle cross-check.
notes: RESOLVED design basis (worklog 066). The d>=2 over-determined dm x (m+1) stacking is SOUND but needs GRACEFUL REDUCTION (not throw, not redesign). Math: exact 1-D null space exists iff components share a genuine degree-m denominator (Mano-Tsuda 'unique iff rank=m', tex:1427); else smallest-σ vector is a legitimate least-squares 'best shared Q'; for entire/far-from-pole components the stack is numerically rank-deficient at the stepper's large m (numpy: eff-rank ~9-10 << m+1=16 at m=15). FIX = GGT's own prescription (GGT2013 md:136, σ_n=0 => reduce n->ρ): replace the ρ>=m_cur break (:208) + dead n_near>1 guard (:224) with a real σ2/σ1 isolation test; reduce m to the honest isolated-1D-null-space degree; throw (Rule 1) only if NO degree isolates. The current Q(0)≈0 throw after a forced reduction is a Rule-1 OVER-throw. Must be re-derived AFTER the +2 window fix (window shift moves every A_full row). reduce-vs-throw decision => REDUCE.

title: P3 — Pade-aware analytical honest-disc estimator (computable formula)

Translate the P1 theory + P2 empirical map into a computable per-node honest-region estimator that takes O(1)-ish time per node (cheap enough for production). Candidate forms: (a) honest radius = distance to (k+1)-th nearest Q-root with small exclusions around the first k = degree(Q) modeled poles; (b) anisotropic radius r(theta) defined by 'next-pole distance in direction theta'; (c) Hermite-like contour formula. title: EPIC: Pade-aware honest-disc gate (extend the truncation-limited B1 ceiling)
description: The current B1 honest-disc gate (src/VectorPathNetworkStage2._validity_radius) uses the Jorba-Zou TAYLOR truncation radius s(tol)*h_JZ*h_v + the pole-adjacency clamp 0.5*h_v*min|t*|. The Jorba-Zou term is 100% binding (S5-diag: 4737/4737 nodes truncation-limited) and saturates near N=48 at ~0.36*D_z asymptotically. ROOT CONCEPTUAL ISSUE (ADR-0026 Amendment 9 / user-surfaced): the gate treats the Pade as if it were the Taylor jet. A Pade approximant's whole point is reach PAST singularities — its denominator Q's zeros model the nearby poles, so the honest region extends past them, bounded by the next UNMODELED singularity. The honest region is likely ANISOTROPIC (a flower, not a disc — wider away from the nearest pole). Implementing a Pade-aware gate could meaningfully grow the certified region and shrink the extrapolated overlay in the headline figure (Option B). Six-phase plan P1-P6: theory -> empirical ring reference -> analytical estimator -> validation -> integration -> re-render. Open-ended research; uncertain magnitude of payoff. Reference: Stahl's theorem on Pade convergence for meromorphic functions; de Montessus de Ballore.

title: P2 — Reference empirical ring-residual estimator (ground truth)

Build a slow-but-correct reference: at a sample of walk nodes, evaluate the stored Pade (P/Q) on a polar grid of test points at varying radii r and angles theta. For each test point compute the local ODE residual (or the disagreement vs an independently-computed reference value at that point — e.g. an adjacent node's Pade if available, or a high-precision retry). The set {r,theta : residual <= tol} is the empirical honest region — the ground truth a production estimator must approximate. Output: a per-node 'honest region map' for a sample of inner/mid/outer wedge nodes; the typical shape (disc, flower, kidney?); the typical area ratio vs the current B1 gate's circular disc. Probe-style; instrumented but src/ byte-identical.

title: P1 — Theory & literature: where is a Pade approximant honestly valid?

Search references/ for in-tree material; supplement from web/literature if needed. title: DEEP-DIVE + PLAN FIRST — senior-grade re-resolution of the P_I^(2) tritronquée surface figure
description:
The whole-plane KKG 7.4/7.5 surface figure (figures/kkg_pi2_tritronquee_surface.jl, worklog 057) is shipped but LOW-RESOLUTION and its pole-wedge render is coarse/blocky. This is a DEEP-DIVE: produce a senior-grade plan (an ADR) BEFORE writing any code. Do NOT just crank grid/target numbers — investigate the real numerical-analysis problem (faithfully rendering a meromorphic transcendent over a region densely packed with poles).

DIAGNOSIS (worklog 057 §'Required follow-up' has the full version):
- Wedge walk: surf_wedge_targets() = SURF_TARGET_RADII (2,4,6,8) x SURF_TARGET_ANGLES (5 angles) = 20 targets, ALL |x|<=8 — copied verbatim from V8b's pole-SCATTER figure (which only needed pole locations). ~389 visited nodes.
- Figure window is |x|<=20 -> MORE THAN HALF the wedge is pure Padé EXTRAPOLATION (surf_wedge_fill uses extrapolate=true — approximants evaluated outside their valid disc — NOT senior-grade).
- Stage-2 fill = nearest-visited-node, gated at the STEP h=0.1 (SURF_PN_H), not the Padé's true radius of convergence -> coarse Voronoi tessellation -> blocky.
- Smooth sector: SURF_GRID_N=121 (121^2 over [-20,20]^2), 6deg ray fan (SURF_RAY_DPHI_DEG) — low-res but cheap to fix.

OPEN QUESTIONS THE PLAN/ADR MUST RESOLVE:
1. Stage-2 validity gating gates at the step h, not the Padé's actual convergence radius (distance to the nearest shared-Q denominator root = nearest pole). Gating at the true radius lets each node cover a far larger in-disc region -> far fewer nodes for full coverage. Investigate — this may be the single biggest lever.
2. The wedge walk density/extent: pole density grows with |x|; estimate the node count to tile |x|<=20; is it tractable? It almost certainly needs bead 0ln.23 (shared-Q root-distance step criterion) — a long walk through a dense pole field will land a fixed-h step on a pole and degenerate.
3. Stage-2 interpolation: nearest-node is blocky; blend overlapping in-disc approximants for C0/C1 continuity?
4. Is pixel-perfect wedge resolution even the right GOAL? KKG's own surface shows the wedge as 'jagged' (they did not finely resolve it). The faithful deliverable may be the pole SCATTER (V8b cleanly extracted 21 poles) over a clamped |u| heatmap. The plan must define what 'faithful + senior-grade' means here, citing KKG 2015 Figs 7.4/7.5.
5. The ray-fan voter is bilinear-interpolated onto the Cartesian grid — at high res its interpolation error may dominate the majority vote; should it be harmonically reconstructed like the 2D-Cheb / Gridap voters?
6. The +/-3deg Stokes-strip masking (STITCH_MASK_DEG) — can those strips be filled?
7. Performance: a dense walk + dense grid must stay tractable.

CONSTRAINTS: senior-grade only (CLAUDE.md Rule 9 — no 'good enough for now'). Every current v1 corner (extrapolate-outside-disc; |x|<=8 hull; 121^2 grid; +/-3deg mask; bilinear ray-fan voter; hand-tuned h=0.1) must be RETIRED or justified with rigour. KKG 2015 Figs 7.4/7.5 + the FW figure conventions are the ground truth (references/). The triple-method majority vote stays. WORKFLOW: deep-dive recon -> ADR with the chosen approach -> granular child beads -> serial Opus implementation -> re-verify. 0ln.23 folds in as a near-certain prerequisite.
acceptance_criteria: (1) A deep-dive recon + an ADR selecting the re-resolution approach, with every v1 corner retired or rigorously justified. (2) A granular child-bead plan. (3) Then: a re-resolved headline figure — no Padé evaluated outside its valid disc, full |x|<=20 wedge coverage, high resolution, KKG-7.4/7.5-faithful, triple-method-voted.
close_reason: Headline-figure re-resolution COMPLETE (ADR-0025 + 12 amendments, worklog 058). 20 child beads across Phases A-F. All six v1 corners retired or rigorously justified; wedge rescoped to a 266-pole FW-validated pole field (filled surface proven infeasible by the A2 spike); seven-criterion FW-style validation suite (VC-4..VC-10) — KKG drew no poles so there is no external oracle. title: F1 — generalise pI2_tritronquee_ic to general complex rays on the V_0 sheet
description: pI2_tritronquee_ic is currently negative-real-axis-only (throws for Re(x0)>=0). The whole-plane KKG 7.4/7.5 surface needs the asymptotic seed on rays x=xi*exp(i*phi) across the V_0 pole-free sector. Branch (KKG: 'analytically continue the cubic root not to be branched in the sector near the negative real axis'): theta = angle(x0)<0 ? angle(x0)+2pi : angle(x0), so theta in [0,2pi); Y = -cbrt(6)*abs(x0)^(1/3)*exp(i*theta/3). On the negative real axis theta=pi -> Y=+cbrt(6)*r^(1/3)>0 (must reproduce the current output EXACTLY). Derivatives simplify: Y'=Y/(3*x0), so leading-order y2=Y/(3x0), y3=-2Y/(9x0^2), y4=10Y/(27x0^3) — rational in Y and x0, no branch tracking for the derivatives. The n_terms=2 c_6 correction Y^(-6) and its x-derivatives likewise. Keep a |x0| large-enough guard.

title: VectorBVP separatrix isolation — Newton globalization + continuation to reach the P_I^(2) tritronquée
description: V8b BLOCKER. The P_I^(2) tritronquee is a separatrix in the 4-param solution family; the current VectorBVP v1 (plain Chebyshev-Newton) cannot isolate it. Empirical findings from the V8b build agent (verified across segments [-20,-2],[-20,-12],[-20,-18],[-30,-20],[-40,-30],[-50,-40] and N in {40,60,80,128}): (1) The 2+2 endpoint-value BC split (pin u,u' at each end from the asymptotic series) is well-conditioned but Newton — even started from the tritronquee series guess — slides off to a different P_I^(2) solution (u swings positive +1.6..+6.5; tritronquee is ~-4.9). ODE residual ~1e-12, so these are genuine solutions, just the wrong branch. (2) Full-asymptotic-state-at-one-end BC (B_a=I,B_b=0) is structurally ill-conditioned: cond ~1e16-1e19, two near-zero singular values (the separatrix growing mode). (3) Forward IVP from the seed diverges immediately (confirms the separatrix instability). KKG 2015 used 512-1024 collocation points + Newton-Armijo line search + careful asymptotic truncation. Likely real fix: globalized Newton (Armijo line search) + a continuation/homotopy driver (start on a short interval where the tritronquee basin is wide, lengthen toward the asymptotic regime tracking the root). This is a v1-corner lift per CLAUDE.md Rule 9 — VectorBVP v1 is honest for non-separatrix vector BVPs.
design: Likely a new VB phase: (a) Newton-Armijo globalization in vector_bvp_solve (or a strict-vs-globalized kwarg); (b) a continuation driver that tracks the tritronquee root as the segment lengthens / a parameter homotopes. Cross-check the converged solution against the KKG asymptotic on the negative real axis.
acceptance_criteria: vector_bvp_solve (or a continuation wrapper) converges to the P_I^(2) tritronquee: u matches -cbrt(6)*|x|^(1/3) on the negative real axis to KKG ~1e-6; verified against the asymptotic series. Unblocks the V8b figure.
notes: PROBE VERDICT (external/probes/pi2-tritronquee-bvp/, Opus probe): (1) vector_bvp_solve is SOUND at d=4 — linear d=4 / 2+2-split sanity test: solErr ~1e-15, BC residual exactly 0.0, endpoint↔node mapping correct. No solver bug. (2) The prior 'violates its own BCs' claim is FALSE — the wrong-branch P_I^(2) solution DOES satisfy the (u,u') boundary data exactly (BC residual 0.0); it is a genuine *different* P_I^(2) solution. (3) The fix prescribed in this bead's title (Armijo + continuation) is DISPROVEN — interval continuation, damped/Armijo Newton, and seeding the KKG asymptotic at every node with N up to 256 ALL slide to the wrong branch. ROOT CAUSE: P_I^(2)'s dominant balance 40u^3≈-240x has TWO real branches for x<0 — u≈-cbrt(6)|x|^(1/3) (the tritronquee) and u≈+cbrt(6)|x|^(1/3) (a distinct genuine solution family); both solve the 2+2-value-BC BVP; the +branch has the dominant Newton basin; the tritronquee is not even a stable fixed point of the collocation-Newton map under pointwise (u,u') endpoint BCs. RECOMMENDED BUILD APPROACHES (untried): (a) asymptotic-series collar matching — least-squares-fit the solution to the many-term truncated series on a BAND of nodes near each end (KKG's actual method, Nc=512-1024); (b) deviation variable v=u+cbrt(6)|x|^(1/3) recast; (c) deflation — compute the easy +branch, deflate it from the residual operator, re-run Newton. BigFloat sharpens but does not change basin structure.
close_reason: MISDIAGNOSIS — closed. The recipe-finding probe (external/probes/pi2-tritronquee-bvp/ step9-12 + RECIPE.md) found the blocker is NOT a separatrix / branch-selection problem and NOT a VectorBVP defect. Root cause: a SIGN ERROR in pI2_tritronquee_ic (src/PainleveHierarchy.jl:466). P_I^(2) leading balance u^3=-6x gives u>0 on the negative real axis (u^3=6|x|>0); the IC returns the negative branch u=-cbrt(6)|x|^(1/3), which has ODE residual ~-9600 at x=-20 — not a solution. Every prior agent pinned the BVP to non-solution values. With the correct (positive) sign, plain vector_bvp_solve converges in 2-3 Newton iterations (residual 1.5e-11, matches KKG series to 1.4e-6). Real fix tracked in the new sign-fix bead. Orchestrator independently verified the arithmetic.

title: v0.2 VB1 — VectorBVP.jl: first-order vector-system Chebyshev-Newton BVP solver
description: New module src/VectorBVP.jl: boundary-value solver for first-order vector ODE systems y'=f(z,y), y:[z_a,z_b]subset C -> C^d, with general linear BC B_a y(z_a)+B_b y(z_b)=g. Chebyshev collocation + Newton, mirroring the proven structure of scalar src/BVP.jl but block-structured for d components. Jacobian df/dy obtained by autodiff (TaylorSeries Taylor1 jets, no new dependency) with optional caller-supplied Jf override. Needed because the P_I^(2) tritronquee is a separatrix (forward IVP diverges; bead padetaylor-r2m) and KKG 2015 used a collocation BVP. ADR-0023 written first (Law 1).
design: First-order vector system collocation: unknown Y is (N+1)xd node values; residual R=D1*Y - s*F where s=(z_b-z_a)/2 and F is the rowwise RHS; tau-method replaces d collocation rows with the d linear-BC rows (exact choice pinned by linear oracle). Newton J*dY=R, J=(D1 kron I_d) - s*blkdiag(Jf(z_j,Y_j)); step-norm convergence ||dY||_inf<=tol. Barycentric vector callable sol(z)->Vector. Generic in T (Float64 + BigFloat-256). Port _chebyshev_D1 (do not reach into BVP.jl privates). <=200 effective LOC.

title: Loop-closure consistency probe on FFW Fig 1 (path-network architecture)
description:
Investigation: the path-network is a tree, so accumulated truncation error along each unique IC-to-leaf path causes visible discontinuities at seams (e.g., FFW Fig 1's spiral-pole-line panel). Hypothesis (user, 2026-05-16): every loop should agree modulo branch cuts. Loop closures supply consistency checks AND a correction signal.

Probe goals:
1. Reuse Fig 1's solve. Build Delaunay tessellation on visited_z. Per non-tree edge: evaluate both endpoints' stored Padés at their midpoint; compute |u_A(M) - u_B(M)|.
2. Topological awareness: only compare nodes with matching visited_sheet tuple.
3. Output: histogram of midpoint disagreements; spatial map of high-disagreement edges; correlation with Fig 1 seam locations.
4. Tree-path-length analysis: identify 'shortcut' edges where adjacent-in-z nodes have long tree-path-distance — these are where accumulated error is most visible.

Deliverables: external/probes/loop-closure-fig1/{Project.toml, probe.jl, REPORT.md, output PNGs}. NOT a src/ change — diagnostic only.

Outcome decides next architectural step:
- If midpoint disagreement correlates with visible seam: graph-consensus Stage-2 (averaging in visited_h neighbourhood) likely fixes most artefact (cheap).
- If midpoint disagreement is small but seam is visible: artefact is elsewhere (rendering interp, sheet bookkeeping); probe gives null result and saves us from misdirected work.

title: lattice_dispatch_solve throws on plain-IVP-corrupted BCs in smooth sectors
description:
SYMPTOM
lattice_dispatch_solve on PI tritronquée at N=121 over [-20,20]² (h_grid=0.333, h_path=0.5, N_bvp=20) throws on the first non-convergent per-row BVP: Newton final ‖Δu‖_∞=0.4458 vs tol=1.8e-12, ‖R‖_∞=169.5 after 10 iterations.  Reproducible via /tmp/smoke_lattice_dispatch.jl from the padetaylor-f8l smoke session.

ROOT CAUSE
Step 1 of lattice_dispatch_solve uses plain path_network_solve over the full grid (no edge gating).  In the pole-free angular sectors (4 of 5 for the tritronquée per FW2011...md:52-54), the plain IVP is walk-tree-seam-corrupted (md:401: 'smooth regions are unstable regions for any IVP solver').  Step 3 then BVP's per-row smooth runs using those corrupted IVP cells as endpoint BCs.  Between two corrupted endpoints across a 30+ unit smooth span there is no self-consistent BVP solution; Newton diverges; lattice_dispatch_solve throws fail-loud (BVP.jl:305).

The throw IS Rule-1-correct fail-loud; the bug is that the lattice composition uses a known-corrupted source as BCs.  Same recipe works fine for FW Fig 4.1 (figures/fw2011_fig_4_1.jl) because there the BVP-spine + IVP-runouts geometry gives clean BCs — the spine is BVP'd, not IVP'd.

PROPOSED FIX
(a) Use edge_gated_pole_field_solve as the IVP source instead of plain path_network_solve. title: EdgeDetector level threshold is grid-fixed; must scale as level₀ + 2·log₁₀(h/h₀)
description:
SYMPTOM
edge_gated_pole_field_solve region-growing stalls at any lattice spacing finer than ~0.25 — the field never grows past the seed disk. Empirically (PI tritronquée, [-20,20]², grow_rings tuned to a ~1-unit frontier):
  h=0.25  (N=161): level=0.001 -> 24 passes, ~18% field  OK
  h=0.125 (N=321): level=0.001 -> STALL (2 passes, seed only); level≈-0.6 -> 21 passes ~18% OK
  h=0.0625(N=641): level=0.001 -> STALL; level=-0.5 -> STALL; level=-1.0 -> 20 passes ~18% OK
The working levels match level = 0.001 + 2·log10(h/0.25) almost exactly (h=0.125 -> -0.60; h=0.0625 -> -1.20).

ROOT CAUSE
EdgeDetector.pole_field_mask thresholds log10|Δu| > level with a fixed default level=0.001; EdgeGatedSolve.edge_gated_pole_field_solve and LatticeDispatcher.lattice_dispatch_solve pass it through as edge_level. But Δu = (5-point stencil · u)/h² of a holomorphic (∴ harmonic) function is O(h²) away from poles — and crucially the pole-*annulus* residual that the flood-fill relies on for cell-to-cell connectivity ALSO scales ~h² (only cells essentially on a pole, d~h, stay ~1/h⁴). So the smooth/annulus floor of log10|Δu| scales as 2·log10(h) + const. A fixed level therefore over-classifies as smooth on fine grids: below spacing 0.25 the connecting annulus drops under 10^level, the flood-fill cannot propagate between adjacent poles, and region growing stalls at the seed.

FW 2011 used a single fixed grid resolution, so a constant 0.001 was correct for them (references/markdown/FW2011_painleve_methodology_JCP230/FW2011_painleve_methodology_JCP230.md:202-208 — '...proportionality constant in the O(h²)...'). The bug is in OUR generalization: we exposed h as a free kwarg but kept level constant. src/EdgeDetector.jl's docstring half-acknowledges this ('calibrated for fine grids', 'Grid resolution matters') but punts it to the caller instead of fixing the scaling — a CLAUDE.md Rule 2 'all bugs are deep' item, not a 'pass edge_level manually' band-aid.

PROPOSED FIX
Make level h-aware: pole_field_mask's default level becomes LEVEL0 + 2·log10(h/H0) with the empirically-calibrated point (H0,LEVEL0)=(0.25,0.001). Keep an explicit level kwarg as an override (e.g. level=:auto sentinel vs a passed Real). Thread the same through edge_gated_pole_field_solve's edge_level and lattice_dispatch_solve. Ground-truth check: confirm FW's own Fig 3.3 grid spacing if recoverable; otherwise our (0.25,0.001) calibration stands and should be documented as such.

AFFECTED
src/EdgeDetector.jl (pole_field_mask), src/EdgeGatedSolve.jl (edge_level passthrough), src/LatticeDispatcher.jl (edge_level), figure scripts hardcoding grids. BLOCKS: the high-resolution headline render (examples/tritronquee_3d.jl at N=641 for a 4x-resolution README hero image) — deferred until this is fixed. The README currently keeps the working N=161 image.
design: Δu smooth-region floor ~ h²; pole-annulus (connectivity-bearing) residual also ~ h²; only d~h cells stay ~1/h⁴. ∴ log10|Δu| floor ∝ 2·log10(h). Fix: level(h) = LEVEL0 + 2·log10(h/H0), calibrated (H0,LEVEL0)=(0.25,0.001) — confirmed by the 3-point sweep above.
acceptance_criteria: edge_gated_pole_field_solve grows correctly (>5 passes, field reaches the expected ~18% tritronquée wedge) at h ∈ {0.25, 0.125, 0.0625} with the DEFAULT level (no manual edge_level); existing EdgeDetector/EdgeGatedSolve/LatticeDispatcher tests stay GREEN, mutation-proven; FW figures 3.3 / 4.1 / 4.7 still reproduce; examples/tritronquee_3d.jl re-renders cleanly at N=641.
close_reason: h-aware auto-scaled level shipped (HEAD 17c284c). 1652/1652 GREEN. N=641 hero render finished cleanly: 92 passes, 75,646-cell field (18.41%), wall 79 min. ADR-0009, worklog 032.

title: Edge-gated pole-field solve — confine IVP path-network to pole fields (FW md:401)
description: FW 2011 md:401: 'smooth regions are unstable regions for any IVP solver ... force the path selection algorithm to complete pole fields before stepping into smooth regions ... with the pole field edge detection procedure (3.2.2) this process can readily be fully automated.' Confirmed empirically: ungated path_network_solve over large regions corrupts the PI tritronquee (spurious poles leak into the 4 pole-free sectors); restricting targets to pole-field cells gives a perfectly sector-confined result. Build edge_gated_pole_field_solve: region-growing solve that starts from a seed near the IC and iteratively expands the targeted cell set ONLY into cells the EdgeDetector (FW 3.2.2) classifies as pole-field, re-running path_network_solve each ring. The IVP never targets deep-smooth cells, so the visited Pade store stays faithful and extract_poles gives a clean pole field. Composes PathNetwork + EdgeDetector. Needed for FW Fig 4.7 panel (f) tritronquee (bead padetaylor-7na).

title: PoleField: extract pole locations from a solved PathNetwork
description: Capability gap flagged in HANDOFF.md: FW 2011 Fig 4.7/4.8 (pole-location plots) need a helper that extracts pole locations from a PathNetworkSolution. Each visited node stores a local Padé approximant P(t)=N(t)/D(t) in the rescaled variable t=(z-z_v)/h; its poles in the z-plane are z_v + h·t_root for roots t_root of D(t). The helper takes the union over all visited nodes, filters spurious/far roots, and deduplicates. Ground truth oracle: the equianharmonic Weierstrass-℘ test problem (u''=6u², FW §5.1.1) whose poles sit on the analytic rhombic lattice z(m,n)=1+2ω(m+n/2)+i·ω√3·n — extracted poles must match this lattice to tolerance. Unblocks the Fig 4.7/4.8 figure reproduction.
design: New module src/PoleField.jl. extract_poles(sol::PathNetworkSolution; radius_t, dedup_atol) -> Vector{Complex{T}}. Uses Polynomials.roots on the denominator b of each visited_pade entry (validated for Complex{Float64}). robust_pade's GGT-2013 SVD rank detection already suppresses Froissart doublets. Radius/dedup defaults pinned empirically against the ℘ lattice per worklog-7 lesson.
acceptance_criteria: extract_poles on a ℘-problem path_network_solve recovers the known rhombic-lattice poles within the covered region to <=1e-6 abs; no spurious poles; mutation-proven (perturb root mapping -> RED).
notes: Shipped src/PoleField.jl + test/polefield_test.jl (22 assertions, mutation-proven M1/M2/M3). extract_poles maps each visited node's Padé denominator roots to the z-plane (z=z_v+h*t*), filters by radius_t/min_residue/cross-node-support, clusters greedily in increasing |t*|. title: PathNetwork: adaptive Padé step size

The current PadeStepper uses fixed h (FW 2011 default 0.5). Adding adaptive h would let path_network_solve concentrate steps near poles and stretch in smooth regions. title: PathNetwork: add enforce_real_axis_symmetry kwarg
description: path_network_solve's shuffle(rng, targets) breaks y-symmetry of the visited tree even when the ODE has real coefficients and ICs are real. For such cases the mathematically correct behaviour is u(z̄) = ū(z), but Stage-2 nearest-visited lookup landing on non-conjugate nodes cascades 4-5 orders of magnitude into |u| at conjugate-pair grid cells (worklog 014, examples/tritronquee_3d.jl shows the fix in user space). Add an opt-in kwarg  that: (a) filters targets to upper-half + on-axis; (b) walks those only; (c) populates lower-half grid_u/grid_up via conj(grid_u_upper). Bit-exact y-symmetric; ~2× faster on full-plane fills. Inapplicable for non-real ICs / complex-coefficient ODEs — leave as opt-in.
