title: Phase 14: SheetTracker — sheet index + branch-cut routing for PVI (FFW 2017 §2.3)
description: Tier-5 architectural wrapper over PathNetwork + CoordTransforms. PVI has two fixed singularities (z=0, z=1); no single coordinate transform avoids both. Solution: tag each path with a Riemann-sheet index s ∈ ℤ tracking winding-number accumulation around each branch point; deliberately circumambulate (clockwise or counterclockwise) via constrained wedge directions. Cross-sheet evaluations forbidden without explicit cross_branch=true (CLAUDE.md Rule 1 fail-fast). References: FFW2017_painleve_riemann_surfaces_preprint.md:163-189 (the circumambulation algorithm), :180-189 (sheet bookkeeping). Depends on: CoordTransforms (Phase 13). Unblocks: figure_catalogue.md §5 Tier-5 figures (FFW2017 Fig 2, 3, 7 — PVI multi-sheet).
close_reason: Phase 14 SheetTracker shipped: src/SheetTracker.jl with ζ-plane PVI RHS + winding-number primitives. 7 testsets / 26 assertions; mutations O+P+Q bit as predicted. End-to-end direct-vs-transformed agreement ≤1e-10. η-plane PVI eq. + constrained-wedge PathNetwork routing deferred (no in-tree caller blocked).

title: Phase 13: CoordTransforms — exponential coordinates for PIII/PV (FFW 2017 §2.1-2.2)
description: Tier-4 architectural wrapper. For PIII: z = e^(ζ/2), u(z) = e^(-ζ/2) w(ζ); strip width 4π in ζ-plane = one z-sheet. For PV: z = e^ζ; strip width 2π. The transformation maps fixed branch points at z=0 (and z=∞ for PV) out of the finite plane, letting the unmodified PathNetwork/BVP run in ζ. Multi-sheet z-plane output recovered by partitioning ζ-plane into strips and applying inverse transform. References: FFW2017_painleve_riemann_surfaces_preprint.md:40-48 (the transformation itself), :67-71 (non-uniform Stage-1 nodes needed because pole density grows exponentially in Re ζ). Depends on: PathNetwork (padetaylor-1jf), Dispatcher (Phase 12 bead just filed). Unblocks: figure_catalogue.md §5 Tier-4 figures (FFW2017 Fig 1, 4, 5, 6). Note: non-uniform Stage-1 nodes are a co-prerequisite — file separately if substantial.
close_reason: Phase 13 CoordTransforms shipped: src/CoordTransforms.jl with PIII/PV exponential transforms + IC helpers; 23 assertions across 6 testsets; mutations L+M+N bit as predicted. End-to-end direct-vs-transformed agreement ≤1e-10. Non-uniform nodes + adaptive Padé h deferred (independent of transform; no downstream caller asking).

title: Friction recorded — GenericLinearAlgebra pirates into LinearAlgebra.svd!

title: Decide: sheet bookkeeping = cut-crossing counter vs analytic continuation (61um follow-on)
description: ADR-0031 §Open: BranchTracker's sheet law (sign(winding_delta) on segment_crosses_cut) is a CUT-CROSSING topological counter. It can diverge from the multivalued solution's ACTUAL analytic-continuation sheet when the chosen cut_angle does not match the function's true branch cut (e.g. cut_angle=π vs sqrt(1-z²)'s rightward cut from z=+1). No current consumer relies on the distinction. Decide which semantics the package should track (likely an ADR), and whether to add a corpus fixture with a genuine sheet-FLIPPING real walk (endpoints straddling the real axis right of z=1) so visited_sheet=[1] is the actual continuation truth.

title: v2: IVPBVP hybrid PFS-vs-BVP derivative glue match to FFW md:247 (~1e-7) — needs BF-256 + n_terms>=15

title: BVP callable contract: disc (|t*|≤1) vs strict segment (Im(t*)≈0) — and BVP/VectorBVP docstring disagreement
description: The padetaylor-53tu fix made both callables guard the documented pre-image DISC |t*|≤1+100eps (Rule 2: root-cause the real(t*) vs |t*| bug; honour the deliberately-documented 'pre-image disc' in BVP.jl:133). TWO follow-on questions deferred from that fix: (1) STRICTER GUARD? The disc still admits off-real-axis interior points (e.g. t*=0.5i, |t*|=0.5≤1) where the spectral interpolant silently EXTRAPOLATES off the real segment — the BVP solution is only defined ON the segment (real t*∈[-1,1]). A maximally-rigorous reading (Rule 1 'silent extrapolation unsafe', which the same docstring asserts) would tighten to imag(t*)≈0 AND |Re t*|≤1 with a scale-aware imag tol. No production caller or test hits the disc-interior off-axis region (verified), so this is a contract-design decision, not a live bug. (2) DOC INCONSISTENCY: BVP.jl documents the 'pre-image disc'; VectorBVP.jl said 'outside the segment' (now aligned to disc phrasing in the 53tu fix). If (1) tightens to the segment, both docstrings + the guard change together (ADR-worthy). Surfaced 2026-06-13.

title: Migrate Statistics from [deps] to [weakdeps] (extension-only stdlib dep)
description: Aqua.stale_deps (bead krgy.2) correctly flags Statistics as unused by the core module: it is consumed ONLY by ext/PadeTaylorDiagnosticsExt.jl:142 (median/quantile/mean over loop-closure edge stats). Per ADR-0003's minimal-core-dep-graph principle it should be a [weakdeps], not a hard [deps]. BLOCKER (non-trivial, why deferred): moving it to weakdeps requires adding Statistics as a CO-TRIGGER of PadeTaylorDiagnosticsExt (Julia errors otherwise: 'extension does not have Statistics in its dependencies'). But a co-trigger changes the documented activation contract — verified empirically (krgy.2 session): with the co-trigger, the extension activates only when BOTH 'using DelaunayTriangulation' AND 'using Statistics' are in the session; DelaunayTriangulation does NOT transitively load Statistics into the trigger set. That regresses ADR-0016's documented 'using PadeTaylor, DelaunayTriangulation' single-trigger UX. Options to weigh: (a) accept the dual-trigger and update ADR-0016 + all diagnose-using tests/docs to add 'using Statistics'; (b) drop the Statistics dependency by inlining the 3 trivial stats (median/quantile/mean) into the extension; (c) keep status quo + Aqua allow-list (current state). Currently allow-listed in test/quality_test.jl via Aqua.test_all(...; stale_deps=(ignore=[:Statistics],)). file:ext/PadeTaylorDiagnosticsExt.jl:142 + Project.toml deps/extensions.
notes: Cross-coupling (krgy.6): test/convergence_test.jl now does 'using Statistics' for its slope fit. When migrating Statistics [deps]->[weakdeps], ALSO add Statistics to [extras]/[targets].test (or inline the ~5-line least-squares), else convergence_test breaks under Pkg.test.

Not a bug: it is the honest shared-Q accuracy for pole-free systems. The v0.2 Painlevé/Calogero targets are MEROMORPHIC (have movable poles) so this does not affect them, but V4/V5/V6 test tolerances on any pole-free sub-case must account for it. Documented in test/vector_stepper_test.jl VS.1.2 comment.
notes: Bug-sweep 2026-06-01 / worklog 065: the ~4e-12 'honest' shared-Q residual on entire/pole-free vector systems is LIKELY a symptom of the SharedPade off-by-one (padetaylor-d3a) and/or the full-column-rank rank-break (padetaylor-3p9c), NOT genuinely honest. title: A7: feedback-driven path-network refinement (extends A1+A2 with post-hoc quality feedback)
description:
Blocked by src/Diagnostics.jl (P2 above).  The natural third axis after A1 (per-step adaptive h) and A2 (initial-mesh non-uniform nodes): post-hoc adaptation based on quality_diagnose feedback.

Algorithm sketch:
  sol = path_network_solve(prob, targets; ...)
  loop:
    report = quality_diagnose(sol)
    exit if report.p99(ΔP_rel) < target_quality
    new_targets = report.recommend_refinement()  # midpoints of Cat-A edges
    sol = path_network_solve(prob, new_targets; warm_start = sol, ...)

title: 2D elliptic Laplace BVP for analytic smooth-region fill
description:
CONTEXT
The Painlevé transcendents are complex-analytic in their pole-free sectors.  Any complex-analytic function u(z) over the (x,y) plane satisfies ∇²u = 0 (the real 2D Laplacian of its real and imaginary parts both vanish — Cauchy-Riemann).  So in a pole-free smooth region with Dirichlet BCs on its boundary, u(x,y) is the unique harmonic function with those BCs.  This is a classical 2D elliptic BVP, fundamentally cleaner than the per-row 1D BVP approach (sibling bead padetaylor-8dg).

This bead is the more principled alternative to padetaylor-8dg.  Both produce a filled smooth region from boundary data; the 2D version is globally consistent (the per-row version can have inter-row discontinuities at the wedge boundary), handles corner-shaped sector geometry naturally (the per-row version requires bilateral flanking), and reduces to a single sparse linear solve per smooth connected component.

PROPOSED API
New function (probably src/SmoothFill2D.jl):

  smooth_fill_2d(u_grid, mask, xs, ys; outer_bc) -> Matrix{Complex{T}}

  - u_grid :: Matrix{Complex{T}}  -- input grid; mask=true cells are taken as given (Dirichlet BC), mask=false cells overwritten
  - mask   :: BitMatrix           -- true = boundary/source (from edge-gated IVP), false = unknown
  - outer_bc :: (z) -> u OR :asymptotic_PI etc. -- BC at the grid edge cells that are mask=false

Algorithm:
  - For each connected component of mask=false cells:
    * Identify boundary cells (neighbours of mask=true cells AND grid-edge cells).
    * Assemble sparse 5-point Laplace operator on the interior cells.
    * RHS from Dirichlet BCs (mask=true neighbours from u_grid; grid-edge from outer_bc).
    * Solve once via sparse LU.  Fill the interior cells with the result.
  - Returns the full grid with all cells populated.

The same machinery generalises to any complex-analytic ODE solution.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- PI tritronquée at [-20,20]² rendered with smooth_fill_2d:
  * Continuous |u| values across the wedge boundary (no harsh -1 floor; no walk-tree seams).
  * Asymptotic recovered at grid edges with outer_bc=:asymptotic_PI.
  * Visually clean — Painlevé-2-style smooth gradient across the four pole-free sectors.
- New test/smooth_fill_2d_test.jl with mutation-proven assertions.
- Headline render examples/tritronquee_3d.jl uses smooth_fill_2d for the smooth sectors.

REJECTED ALTERNATIVES
- 'Per-row 1D BVP (padetaylor-8dg)' — simpler but inter-row inconsistent and can't handle non-bilateral runs.  Keep as a lower-cost fallback.
- 'Plain path_network_solve over the whole grid' — has walk-tree seams (demonstrated in /tmp/smoke_plain_full_solve.png from the padetaylor-f8l smoke session).
- 'Lattice dispatcher with corrected BCs' — its per-row geometry can't fill the half-bounded outer rim regardless of BC quality.

DEPENDENCIES
- Useful but not required: padetaylor-8dg's asymptotic factories (asymptotic_PI, asymptotic_PII, ...) — if shipped first, smooth_fill_2d can reuse them rather than reimplementing.
- Independent of: padetaylor-f8l (the EdgeDetector fix), edge_gated_pole_field_solve (this consumes its output, doesn't modify it).

NOTES
- Probably the right long-term answer for headline renders of any Painlevé transcendent.  PII / PIV / etc. just plug in their own asymptotic.
- Performance: a single sparse LU on the smooth-component cells.  At N=641 / [-20,20]² with ~80% smooth coverage that's ~330k unknowns — well within sparse-direct-solver capacity (LU on a 5-point stencil graph is essentially free).

Refs: padetaylor-8dg (1D per-row variant, the lighter alternative); padetaylor-f8l worklog 032 (the smoke session that surfaced the gap); src/EdgeGatedSolve.jl (the IVP source for the inner BCs); references/markdown/FW2011_painleve_methodology_JCP230/FW2011_painleve_methodology_JCP230.md:42-55 (PI asymptotic).

title: bvp_fill_with_asymptotic: 1D per-row BVP using algebraic asymptotic as outer BC
description:
CONTEXT
Most smooth-sector rows in a tritronquée-style headline render are NOT bilaterally flanked by IVP cells — they reach the grid edge on one (or both) sides with the smooth/pole-free sector wide open.  The existing per-row bvp_solve in lattice_dispatch_solve needs BCs at both ends and so leaves those cells either at their (corrupted) plain-IVP values or, post the sibling bug fix, tagged :ivp_only.

The Painlevé equations have known leading-term algebraic asymptotics in their pole-free sectors that act as natural outer BCs.  For Painlevé I, the Boutroux asymptotic is u(z) ~ -sqrt(-z/6) at large |z| in the pole-free regime (FW2011...md:42-55, used in figures/fw2011_fig_4_1.jl step (i) as the leading() function).  PII, PIV have their own (FW2014 etc.).

PROPOSED API
New function (probably src/AsymptoticFill.jl, or as a new method on bvp_solve):

  bvp_fill_with_asymptotic(prob, asymptotic, xs, ys; mask, inner_bcs, N_bvp=20) -> Matrix{Complex{T}}

  - asymptotic :: (z) -> u  -- the algebraic asymptotic for the equation (PI: z -> -sqrt(-z/6))
  - mask       :: BitMatrix -- true = pole-field (skip), false = smooth (fill)
  - inner_bcs  :: Matrix{Complex{T}} -- IVP values at mask=true cells (from edge_gated)

For each smooth row j:
  - Find contiguous false-runs in mask[:, j]
  - For each run [i_lo, i_hi]:
    * Outer BCs: asymptotic(z(i_lo, j)) or inner_bcs[i_lo-1, j] (whichever exists)
    * Inner BCs: similarly on the high end
    * bvp_solve over the run
  - Returns the filled u_grid (smooth cells now BVP-resolved)

For PII / PIV / other Painlevés the same shape generalises — just plug in the relevant asymptotic.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- PI tritronquée at [-20,20]² rendered with bvp_fill_with_asymptotic over the four pole-free sectors:
  * Values continuous across the wedge boundary (rel_err < 1e-4 vs edge-gated IVP at boundary cells).
  * Asymptotic recovered at grid edge (rel_err < 1e-6 vs asymptotic(z) at outer cells).
- New test/asymptotic_fill_test.jl with mutation-proven assertions.
- Demo figure: examples/tritronquee_3d.jl re-rendered with the smooth sectors BVP-filled (no -1 display floor, no walk-tree seams).

REJECTED ALTERNATIVES
- 'Use a coarser BVP grid' — doesn't help, the issue is missing one BC, not resolution.
- '2D elliptic BVP for the whole sector' — sibling bead, more principled but more work.  This bead is the lighter-weight variant.

NOTES
- This is purely additive (new function); no impact on existing IVP / lattice_dispatch / edge_gated APIs.
- Couples loosely with the asymptotic functions already in figures/fw2011_fig_4_1.jl — that script's leading(z) = -sqrt(-z/6) is the per-equation factory we'd lift into a public asymptotic_PI helper.

Refs: figures/fw2011_fig_4_1.jl (existing 1D asymptotic-BC example); references/markdown/FW2011_painleve_methodology_JCP230/FW2011_painleve_methodology_JCP230.md:42-55.

title: Closed-form named Painleve families: PII rational/Airy, PIV entire (exact oracles)

These differ in shape from the point-IC named transcendents: they are parametrized families (pii_rational(n), pii_airy(theta)) AND they come with EXACT closed-form oracles, which makes them ideal self-validating tests (solver output cross-checked against the exact formula). Deferred from v1 because the parametrized-family API + closed-form-oracle test pattern deserves its own ADR treatment. Out of scope: PIV Generalized Hermite/Okamoto rationals (formulas not in-tree, cite Clarkson 2006).

title: F64 long-range accuracy: close the 600-25000× gap vs FW Padé
description: At Float64 z=30 we get rel-err 4.46e-11 vs FW's 7.62e-14 (600×); at z=10⁴ we get 6.05e-6 vs FW's 2.34e-10 (25,000×). BF-256 we BEAT FW (worklog 008), so algorithm is correct — gap is F64-specific roundoff. Worklog 019 enumerates attack vectors: (1) route F64 through GenericLinearAlgebra Jacobi SVD instead of LAPACK Demmel-Kahan; (2) Kahan-summed Horner in _evaluate_pade / _evaluate_pade_deriv; (3) compensated h^k accumulator (or muladd); (4) study FW's original MATLAB Padé impl (pre-GGT 2013) and port any per-step roundoff tricks. Probe: 10-step wedge walk at 22.5° amplifies O(eps) per-coefficient differences in h^k rescaling to 2.5e-10 in u — concentrated in the step crossing the z=1 lattice pole (~65× amplification alone). Order ≥ 30 saturates Float64 truncation; raising order does NOT close the gap. Suitable for a Phase-15 'accuracy hardening' subproject.
notes: Superseded by the new P1 bead for classical-Padé default in RobustPade.  The four attack vectors listed in this bead's description (Jacobi for F64, Kahan-summed Horner, compensated h^k, port FW's MATLAB Padé) all reduce to a single answer: FW used Toeplitz \ (linear solve, not SVD).  Worklog 020 documents the empirical probe (classical Padé closes the F64 gap to <1e-13 at z=30, <1e-10 at z=10⁴ — better than FW at z=10⁴).  Closing as superseded once the new bead is claimed.
